Name: ChatWithNPCs
Author: songhaifan
Description:
[center][size=5][b]Chat With NPCs[/b][/size]
Say something. I'm giving up on you.[/center]

[line]
In vanilla Stardew Valley, you get [b]one[/b] canned line per villager per day. Then they just stand there. You, watering can in hand, heart full of things to say. Them: "Oh, hey."
Not anymore.
[b]Chat With NPCs[/b] lets you type [i]anything[/i] to a villager and get a real, in-character reply — shown in a normal dialogue box, with the portrait switching to match their mood. Powered by an LLM: [b]local and free[/b], or your own cloud API.
And here's the fun part: they actually [b]know[/b] you. Your name, your friendship level, the season and time, where they're standing, their family, their schedule for the day — all of it feeds the conversation.
So when you walk up to your girlfriend Haley and open with [i]"I like your sister more"[/i]... she remembers you said that.
[quote]Seriously, Frank? That's incredibly rude. Emily's been wonderful to you.[/quote]Go on. Say something. 
[line]
[b]Main features[/b]
[b]💬 Actually talk to them[/b]
Free-text chat, as much as you want. Replies appear as real game dialogue with matching emotion portraits — happy, sad, angry, love.
[b]🧠 They know their world[/b]
Every reply is grounded in the game's own data: your name and gender, your friendship level, the season/day/time/weather, exactly where they are, their daily schedule, their family and relationships, and their canonical line for today — so the AI chat picks up right where the vanilla greeting left off.
[b]🎭 Real personalities[/b]
Every villager has a hand-written character profile. Shane broods. Elliott waxes poetic. Abigail wants to go spelunking.
[b]🌐 Speaks your language[/b]
Replies come back in your game's language automatically, using the official in-game names for people and places.
[b]🔁 Remembers[/b]
Each villager remembers your recent conversation within a play session.
[b]✅ Doesn't wreck vanilla[/b]
Daily dialogue always plays first. NPCs keep their schedules and animations. A little double-speech-bubble cursor shows up when an AI chat is available.

[line]
[b]Requirements[/b]
SMAPI 4.0+
An OpenAI-compatible chat API — pick one:
[list]
[*]Local (recommended): Ollama or LM Studio — free, private, offline[/*]
[*]Cloud: OpenAI, DeepSeek, etc. — needs your own API key[/*]
[/list]Optional: Generic Mod Config Menu for in-game settings
⚠️ You need to set up a model yourself — there's no AI bundled in the mod. It's a free, 5-minute, one-time setup with Ollama. See below.
[line]
[b]Installation instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Install Ollama, then run: ollama pull gemma3:12b (or any chat model you like). It runs quietly in the background.[/*]
[*](Optional) Install Generic Mod Config Menu.[/*]
[*]Unzip this mod into your Stardew Valley/Mods folder.[/*]
[*]Launch the game once via SMAPI, then set your Model (and API URL/key if using cloud) in Generic Mod Config Menu, or edit config.json.[/*]
[*]In game: right-click a villager (daily line plays first — right-click again to chat), or press N. Type, hit Enter, wait a beat for the first reply while the model warms up.[/*]
[/list]Using cloud instead of local? Set ApiUrl, ApiKey, and Model in config. Never share a config.json with a real API key in it.
